column1: # The road from bzip2 `ready` to `passing` -- WP-56's overall done-when.
# WP-56's per-slice clause is met (24/24 live-crossed) and bzip2 reads `ready`:
# it builds, links, and every libc symbol it imports resolves. What stands
# between `ready` and `passing` is not more wiring but a runtime that can start
# a real dynamic program and carry its live calls -- a short ladder of loader
# capabilities the crossing specimens deliberately deferred. This file names
# them, in dependency order. It is a curated roadmap (the denominator), but each
# row's status is derived, never hand-set: bin/progress.py green evaluates the
# `signal` against git truth -- the .smon ledger, the accept verdict, the
# done-when clauses -- so a row flips itself the moment its capability lands.
# Columns, TAB-separated:  id <TAB> signal <TAB> description
# signal grammar (comma-separated alternatives; the row is done if ANY holds):
#   smon:<step>:<state>       a session-monitor step reached a state (e.g. ok)
#   accept:<pkg>:<verdict>    the package's accept verdict is at least <verdict>
#                             (does-not-build < needs-wiring < shape-mismatch < ready < passing)
#   clause:<substring>        a met done-when clause's text contains the substring (case-insensitive)
#   grep:<relpath>:<regex>    the regex matches somewhere in the file
#   -                         no automatic signal yet; the row stays open until one is added
# A signal must be SPECIFIC to this package's road, not a substring that also
# matches an unrelated WP's clause. So these rows key on the code or the verdict
# that proves the capability for bzip2's crossing, and a capability with no
# reliable signal yet carries `-` (stays open) until one is wired -- never a
# generic clause match that another WP would trip.
id
dynamic-crossing
column3: the driver relocates a dynamic image's GOT and PLT against the runtime and enters it (DR-0058); certified on a bzip2-shaped, no-syscall specimen

column1: init-chain
column3: the image's DT_INIT and DT_INIT_ARRAY constructors run across the crossing, in WP-33's load order, before control reaches _start

column1: segment-mapping
column3: bzip2 is linked granule-separable so no two PT_LOAD segments of unlike protection share a 64K NT granule; the loader correctly refuses otherwise (DR-0008), so the fix is build-side (max-page-size >= granule, ideally the toolchain default), not a loader change. bzip2's Makefile sets none, inherited a sub-granule default, and halts before entry (elf_map_err_granule)

column1: reent-tls-bringup
column3: the runtime's reent/TLS structure is set up so libc calls that consult it (errno, the string and locale rows) work at runtime, not merely link; the crossing specimens never set it up (live-string.sh)

column1: syscall-surface
column3: the raw syscall path bzip2's own test suite exercises (the read/write/open a make-test run performs) reaches the host; the dynamic-crossing specimen makes no syscall, that surface being a later package (dyn-cross-spec.S)

column1: run-stage-wired
column3: accept.sh launches the pinned package's own suite through the crossing rather than stopping at `ready` (today its run stage reports what it waits on)

column1: bzip2-passes
column3: bzip2 builds, links, runs its own test suite, and passes it -- WP-56's overall done-when, the terminal gate
